scope: Every reference Cypher query of the pinned LDBC SNB Interactive v1 implementation, mapped to the RushDB GQL profile: `accepted` cases run against the fixture with hand-derived expected results (crates/rushdb-language/tests/gql_ldbc_profile_mapping.rs); `typedUnsupported` cases name the construct and why it is not mapped. Not an audited LDBC benchmark.

cases.statement: MATCH (n:Person {id: $personId})-[:IS_LOCATED_IN]->(p:City) RETURN n.firstName AS firstName, n.lastName AS lastName, n.birthday AS birthday, n.locationIP AS locationIP, n.browserUsed AS browserUsed, p.id AS cityId, n.gender AS gender, n.creationDate AS creationDate

cases.reason: Cypher `WITH … LIMIT` followed by a second MATCH. ISO GQL composes it with NEXT, and the embedded engine's NEXT returns wrong rows (it drops the bound variable and pairs every left row with every right row), so no faithful mapping executes. Engine defect.

cases.reason: shortestPath inside a WITH pipeline: the embedded engine's shortestPath reports no path where one exists (see IC13) and its NEXT composition is defective (see IS2). Engine defects.

cases.reason: Four-stage WITH pipeline (collect, then MATCH over the collection, then aggregation): needs NEXT, defective in the embedded engine (see IS2). Engine defect.

cases.translation: Neo4j :param directives and comments removed. The chained comparison `$startDate <= post.creationDate < $endDate` is written with AND (ISO GQL has no chained comparisons).
cases.statement: MATCH (person:Person {id: $personId })-[:KNOWS]-(friend:Person), (friend)<-[:HAS_CREATOR]-(post:Post)-[:HAS_TAG]->(tag) WITH DISTINCT tag, post WITH tag, CASE WHEN $startDate <= post.creationDate AND post.creationDate < $endDate THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS valid, CASE WHEN post.creationDate < $startDate THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS inValid WITH tag, sum(valid) AS postCount, sum(inValid) AS inValidPostCount WHERE postCount>0 AND inValidPostCount=0 RETURN tag.name AS tagName, postCount ORDER BY postCount DESC, tagName ASC LIMIT 10

WITH aggregation, UNWIND of the collected list, then MATCH: needs NEXT, defective in the embedded engine (see IS2). Engine defect.

Message (the LDBC supertype of Post and Comment) is matched as `x:Post OR x:Comment`: LMPG records carry one label. `WITH collect(distinct friend) … UNWIND` (deduplicating friends before the join) is the same set as one MATCH with RETURN DISTINCT over (friend, message); `ORDER BY message.id` becomes the projected `commentOrPostId`.

cases.reason: collect() of tag ids in a WITH, then a MATCH filtered by membership, over a type-alternation variable-length path (HAS_TYPE|IS_SUBCLASS_OF*0..): needs NEXT, defective in the embedded engine (see IS2). Engine defect.
shortestPath: the embedded engine returns -1 (no path) for two persons joined by a two-hop KNOWS path. Engine defect.
allShortestPaths, list comprehensions with reduce() over pattern comprehensions: refused by the embedded engine's parser, and its shortestPath is defective (see IC13). Engine defect.

After `WITH p, count(*) … UNWIND … MATCH … CREATE`, the embedded engine silently drops every create following the first WITH while reporting success; the statement also matches the Organisation supertype of University and Company, which LMPG's one-label records do not have. Engine defect and data-model exclusion.
After `WITH f UNWIND $tagIds … MATCH … CREATE`, the embedded engine silently drops the HAS_TAG creates while reporting success (only the forum and HAS_MODERATOR are written). Engine defect.

Creates a Post:Message node (two labels: LMPG records carry one), uses CASE inside a property map (refused by the embedded engine with an internal error), and creates HAS_TAG after a WITH/UNWIND (dropped, see IU4). Data-model exclusion and engine defects.
Creates a Comment:Message node (two labels) and matches the Message supertype by a computed id; creates HAS_TAG after a WITH/UNWIND (dropped, see IU4). Data-model exclusion and engine defect.
